parsed_response.reasoning: The diff shows findMembers issues an AJAX request keyed on the group's current offset/limit and, in the then() callback, unconditionally calls self.setProperties({user_count, limit, offset, members}) with the response's values. There is no request token, cancellation, or ordering guard, and the next/previous actions simply set offset and re-call findMembers, so two overlapping requests (rapid next/previous clicks, or removeMember's reload racing a page change) can resolve out of order, and the older response will overwrite newer offset/members state. The mechanism is fully verifiable in the diff: group.set("offset", offset); return group.findMembers(); and the setProperties in the .then callback. This is a real correctness defect (stale state overwriting fresh state), even if the trigger requires a race.

judged_text: findMembers applies whichever response arrives last via setProperties with no request sequencing or cancellation, so overlapping pagination fetches can resolve out of order and overwrite newer offset/members state with older. Rapid next/previous clicks, or a removeMember reload racing a page change, can leave the pager showing one page's member list under another page's indicator until the next interaction re-syncs.
